key_insight: Recurrent neural operators can approximate microstructure-dependent homogenized viscoelastic laws, with a sufficient internal-variable dimension growing logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates aim to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while capturing loading-history and microstructure dependence.
method: Use internal variables to approximate history dependence through a Markovian state.
Learn microstructure-dependent constitutive responses with neural operators.
Use the memory kernel’s spectral representation to prove uniform approximation for periodic Kelvin–Voigt materials in 2D and 3D.
evidence_signal: Viscoelasticity and crystal-plasticity experiments examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity using unit-cell data; the theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees apply to periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity; crystal-plasticity experiments do not establish equivalent guarantees for broader nonlinear inelastic behavior.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
